Phase 3.2 is based on The Matrix: Reloaded movie which in turn is deeply based on the Alice Through the Looking Glass novel. 

The way I came to the conclusion that the novel has something to do with the phase is from this line:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A fubcd-king & oracle-queen, thingky mvps, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

Remove the characters that were used in the alphabet to solve the Vic cipher and your left with this:

"Raising the stakes without extra chances of winning. A -king & -queen, on a sad board but as wide as the first one seen."

This entire text I interpret as having to do with a game of chess and not a straddling checkerboard as some have suggested. What is Alice Through the Looking Glass based on? A literal game of chess.

hey guys, tired of AI? I asked Fable 5 to score out the shittiness of the components of what the author himself refers to as "salphation", and it turns out the entire phase sits on a strong 7 out of 10 shitiness. Here's the breakdown:

—-
SalPhaseIon — an honest component-by-component critique

I scored each piece on an over-engineering / time-sink index (1–10, higher = more needlessly convoluted with less real payoff), based on exhaustive testing with proper controls.

🔴 FAED (570 chars, a–i, undecoded) — 10/10
The black hole. No crib, no verification, no recoverable key. The whole cipher family (base-27, Bifid, Trifid + keyword cubes, all 9! permutations, g-null) tested with controls → noise every time. May be ciphertext from which nothing can be recovered without info that was never given. The cardinal design sin.

🔴 matrixsumlist — 8/10
A noun disguised as an operation. Sends you hunting ~2.4M selector candidates that are pure keyword-tautology (ENTER/NEO/KEY). Bait.

🟠 shabef / anstoo / ourfirsthintisyourlastcommand — 7/10
Cryptic 6-char tokens that are almost certainly just labels/flavor, but eat months of solver attention. (shabef = "SHA before" tested as sha256 → zero effect on the blobs.)

🟠 The two AES blobs ("Yin-Yang structure?") — 6/10
Real, but you can't brute-force them, and the password assembly is under-specified. A design bottleneck, not a skill gap.

🟡 enter (40 a/b bits → "enter") — 5/10
A magnet for false positives on any keyword-scoring tool.

🟡 yellowblueprimes / colored cells — 4/10
Elegant binding, but it just leads back to DBBI = a checkpoint.

🟢 DBBI prime-marker scaffold (b/be on prime positions) — 3/10
The one piece of genuine craftsmanship — provably designed (0 of 300,000,000 shuffles admit a valid prime-marker parse + color match). Not garbage, actually beautiful. Sadly, the only one.

Phase average: ~7/10 over-engineered. One gem (the prime-marker scaffold) buried under a pile of under-specified, unverifiable cruft and labels masquerading as operations.

author: Barend
text:
Buy Entry Modulation allows you the change the bots buy behavior. 

If you want the bot buy a bit earlier you set a positive BEM, so it buys x percentage above the normal buy entry.

If you want the bot to buy a bit later you set a negative BEM, so it buys x percentage below the normal buy entry.

Risk of setting a positive BEM is that if the market goes down the bot may buy a lot. Risk of a negative BEM is that it will set less buys then usual.

author: Barend
text:
BEM puts your buy-order x percent above- or below the normale buy entry.
So compared with the normal buy entry when you put BEM on 3, it will put the buy order 3% higher. As a result it will faster buy.

A negative BEM (-4 for example) does the opposite, it puts buy orders below the original buy entry. So it wil acquire your alt later than usual.

Risk of a positive BEM is that all your funds will be used as it will keeps buying your alt when the charts goes down.

No recommendation but I set positive BEM when the market is ‘stable-ish’ or moving upwards. And sometimes a negative BEM when the market is crashing to prevent too much buys.
